name: London System
tagline: Unshakeable dark-square pyramid, lethal e5 outpost, and kingside attacks.

corePlans: Build the c3-d4-e3 pawn pyramid AFTER getting the dark-squared bishop outside to f4.
Plant a knight on the e5 outpost backed by d4 and f4 (or c3-d4-e5 chain) and swing pieces toward h7.
Welcome ...Bxg3 trades—recapturing hxg3 opens the h-file for a free rook battery.
goldenRules: Never play e3 before Bf4 (don't lock your own bishop inside the hull).
Against ...c5, hold firm with c3—never panic-capture dxc5.
If Black fianchettoes (...g6), play h3 early to build an h2 escape hatch for your bishop.

lines.title: Classical ...d5 & The h-File Hook
lines.subtitle: Your bread-and-butter setup against standard 1...d5 development
lines.frequencyNote: Appears in ~45% of 1000–1600 Rapid games after 1. d4 d5

annotations.plan: Deploy the dark-squared bishop OUTSIDE the pawn chain immediately before closing the door with e3.
annotations.cosmicCue: Launch the probe before sealing the airlock.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing e3 before Bf4 traps your c1 bishop behind your own pawns—you just turned the London into a passive Colle.

annotations.plan: Reinforce d4 with c3 to complete the London pyramid. If Black takes ...cxd4, you recapture exd4 and open the e-file.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Capturing dxc5 gives up your central stronghold and develops Black's bishop for free.

annotations.plan: Retreat to g3! Never trade first with Bxd6. Make Black capture on g3 so hxg3 blasts open your h-file rook.
annotations.cosmicCue: Bait the trade—open the h-file laser cannon.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Trading on d6 helps Black develop their queen to an ideal square while you get zero h-file play.

annotations.plan: Aim the bishop straight at h7 and control the critical e4 and e5 squares. Next up: Ne5 and kingside pressure.

lines.title: Refuting the Early ...Qb6 Raid
lines.subtitle: How to neutralize Black's #1 trick against the London
lines.frequencyNote: Very common anti-London weapon from 1100–1700

annotations.plan: Meet ...Qb6 head-on with Qb3! If Black trades ...Qxb3, axb3 opens your a-file rook and gives you a huge queenside grip.
annotations.cosmicCue: Deflect the raid—never play passive b3.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing b3 weakens your light squares on c3 and a3 permanently. Qb3 defends b2 cleanly with tempo.

annotations.plan: Slide calmly to c2. Black's c4 push released all tension on your d4 pawn, which now lets you prepare a huge e4 central break!
Strike with e4! Because Black released central tension with ...c4 and delayed castling, White blows open the center with advantage.
annotations.cosmicCue: Center breach authorized.

lines.title: Punishing the Copycat (...Bf5)
lines.subtitle: Exploit Black's abandoned b7 pawn immediately
lines.frequencyNote: Frequent surprise at 1000–1400 when Black mirrors you

annotations.plan: Break the symmetry immediately with c4! Black's light-squared bishop just left b7 undefended—switch into Queen's Gambit pressure.
annotations.cosmicCue: Mirror broken. Target b7.

annotations.plan: Launch Qb3! Directly hits the undefended b7 pawn and forces Black into awkward concessions like ...b6 or ...Qc8.

lines.title: The h3 Loft vs King's Indian (...g6)
lines.subtitle: Keep your prized f4 bishop alive against ...Nh5
lines.frequencyNote: Standard fight against King's Indian / Modern setups

annotations.plan: Place the bishop safely on e2 instead of d3 against ...g6 setups—on d3 it risks getting hit by an early ...e5 and ...e4 fork.
Play h3! This prophylactic loft builds an escape hatch on h2 so Black can never hunt down your dark-squared bishop with ...Nh5.
annotations.cosmicCue: Escape pod armed on h2.

counterGuide.title: Early ...c5 & ...Qb6 b2 Raid
counterGuide.keyIdea: Hit White's dark-squared bishop's abandonment of b2 immediately with ...c5 and ...Qb6, grabbing space on the queenside.

counterGuide.title: Immediate ...Bd6 Bishop Trade
counterGuide.keyIdea: Challenge the pride of the London (the f4 bishop) early with ...Bd6, then break with ...c5 for a comfortable game.

name: Modern Defense
tagline: Universal counter-punch vs 1. e4 and 1. d4—let White overextend, then shred their center.

corePlans: Hold back ...Nf6 early so White can't kick your knight with e5 and keep the g7 sniper diagonal wide open.
Expand with ...a6 + ...b5 + ...Bb7 (Tiger's Modern) to kick Nc3 and win the e4 pawn.
Against greedy 3-pawn centers (f4), strike IMMEDIATELY with ...c5 and ...Qa5.
goldenRules: Your g7 bishop is your flagship weapon—never trade it lightly without compensation.
Don't play passively forever: always look for the ...c5, ...b5, or ...e5 pawn break.
If White plays Bh6 to trade your sniper, tuck the bishop or counterattack the center before your dark squares weaken.

lines.title: Tiger's Modern: Double-Fianchetto Crossfire
lines.subtitle: Active queenside expansion that punishes routine White development
lines.frequencyNote: Highest practical win-rate weapon against standard 1. e4 setups

annotations.plan: Play ...d6 before ...Nf6. This stops e5 tricks and keeps the g7 bishop's diagonal completely unobstructed.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Developing ...Nf6 before ...d6 lets White jam e5 immediately, chasing your knight right back home.

annotations.plan: Launch ...a6 (Tiger's Modern)! Stops Nb5/Bb5 annoyances and prepares a rapid ...b5 queenside expansion.
annotations.cosmicCue: Flank thrusters engaged.

annotations.plan: Push ...b5! Claims queenside space and threatens ...b4 to deflect White's c3 knight away from guarding the e4 pawn.
Complete the double fianchetto with ...Bb7! Now both bishops slice across the board, putting e4 and d4 under relentless crossfire.
annotations.cosmicCue: Dual laser lock on e4.

lines.title: Shredding the Greedy f4 Center
lines.subtitle: Punish White's 4. f4 Austrian Attack with an instant ...c5 + ...Qa5 counterpunch
lines.frequencyNote: White's most aggressive try at 1100–1600 Rapid

annotations.plan: Counterattack IMMEDIATELY with ...c5! White pushed f4 instead of developing, leaving their d4 center and e1-a5 diagonal exposed.
annotations.cosmicCue: They overextended—detonate d4.

annotations.plan: Swing out ...Qa5! Pins the c3 knight to the king, prevents White from holding the extra c5 pawn, and puts instant heat on e4.
Recapture ...Qxc5 with comfort! White's big center is shattered, their f4 pawn weakens their king, and your g7 sniper rules the board.

lines.title: Universal Modern vs 1. d4 (Center Strike)
lines.subtitle: Use the exact same ...g6 + ...Bg7 + ...d6 shell against 1. d4, then strike with ...e5
lines.frequencyNote: Zero extra memorization needed against 1. d4 / Queen's Gambit

annotations.plan: Once White commits to c4 and e4, ...Nf6 is completely safe (e5 is no longer a threat because you can answer ...dxe5). Castle fast.
Strike the center with ...e5! Forces White to make a decision: if d5, you launch a kingside pawn storm (...Nh5 + ...f5); if dxe5, your pieces fly out effortlessly.
annotations.cosmicCue: Center clash initiated.

counterGuide.title: Austrian 3-Pawn Center (e4-d4-f4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Punish Black's passive move-order by seizing the entire center with d4, e4, and f4, aiming for an e5 breakthrough.

counterGuide.title: 150 Attack (Be3 + Qd2 + Bh6)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Set up a simple Be3 + Qd2 battery to trade off Black's g7 dragon bishop and launch h4-h5 on the kingside.

name: Anti-London & Zukertort
tagline: Dismantle quiet 1. Nf3 fianchettos and opponent London Systems using active center strikes.

corePlans: Against 1. Nf3 + g3 (Zukertort), grab the center immediately with ...e5 and keep the g7 sniper clear with ...Ne7.
Against the London, prepare ...Nd7 first, then blast ...e5 with tempo and hunt White's dark-squared bishop via ...Nh6–f5.
Against standard 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4, hit immediately with ...c5 and ...Qb6, then clamp the queenside with ...c4.
goldenRules: Against 1. Nf3 (no d4 pawn), claim space with ...e5 instead of playing passively.
Never play ...e5 vs the London before ...Nd7 defends it—or dxe5 Qxd8+ Nxe5 drops a pawn.
When raiding b2 with ...Qb6, never trade queens on b3—push ...c4 to gain space and tempo.

lines.title: Crushing the Zukertort Fianchetto (1. Nf3)
lines.subtitle: Use your ...g6 + ...Bg7 shell to seize the whole center with ...e5
lines.frequencyNote: Direct counter to 1. Nf3 + g3/Bg2 setups at 1100–1600

annotations.plan: Grab the center with ...e5 immediately! Because White played Nf3 and g3 instead of d4, nobody stops you from claiming the best central real estate.
annotations.cosmicCue: Unclaimed territory detected—drop the flag on e5.

annotations.plan: Develop the knight to e7 instead of f6! This keeps your g7 sniper unobstructed and leaves the f-pawn free to storm forward with ...f5 later.
Complete smooth development with ...Nbc6. You have a rock-solid Botvinnik shell controlling d4, ready to launch ...f5 or ...h6 + ...Be6.

lines.title: Modern Counter-Strike vs the London
lines.subtitle: Prep ...e5 with ...Nd7, then hunt the London bishop with ...Nh6–f5
lines.frequencyNote: Keeps your Modern repertoire 100% universal against London players

annotations.plan: Play ...Nd7 first! It defends e5 so you can launch ...e5 cleanly on the very next move without blundering the d-file queen trade.
annotations.cosmicCue: Arm the escort before firing e5.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing ...e5 before ...Nd7 hangs the e5 pawn after dxe5 dxe5 Qxd8+ Kxd8 Nxe5!

annotations.plan: Strike with ...e5! Hits White's prized London bishop with tempo and opens diagonals for your pieces.
Jump ...Nh6! Looks strange, works like magic: it clears the g7 diagonal and heads straight for f5 to eliminate White's g3 bishop.
annotations.cosmicCue: Flank manoeuvre—locking onto the g3 bishop.

lines.title: The ...c5 + ...Qb6 + ...c4 Queenside Clamp
lines.subtitle: Punish passive London players who forget how to handle the ...Qb6 raid
lines.frequencyNote: High-scoring tactical antidote if you prefer 1...d5 vs the London

annotations.plan: Strike b2 immediately with ...Qb6! Forces White to defend awkwardly or walk straight into your ...c4 queenside clamp.
Push ...c4! Never trade queens on b3—shut the queenside door, kick the queen back to c2, and prepare ...Bf5 with massive tempo.
annotations.cosmicCue: Close the blast doors on c4.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Trading queens on b3 hands White a free open a-file for their rook and relieves all pressure on b2.

annotations.plan: Drop ...Bf5 with tempo on White's queen! Black controls the dark squares, has huge queenside space, and dictates the entire middlegame.

counterGuide.title: White's Solid c3 + h3 Pyramid
counterGuide.keyIdea: When Black raids b2 with ...Qb6, White defends cleanly with Nc3/Rb1 or Na4 and fights for central control.

counterGuide.title: Space-Grabbing d5 Push
counterGuide.keyIdea: Push 3.d5! to claim a Benoni-style space advantage; if Black greedily grabs b2, White gets a ferocious lead in development.

name: Jobava London
tagline: Turbo-charged Accelerated London (2. Nc3 + 3. Bf4) packed with c7 fork threats and fast attacks.

corePlans: Combine Nc3 + Bf4 to threaten Nb5 followed by Nxc7+ forking King and Rook.
Even when Black stops Nb5 with ...a6 or ...Na6, their pieces are tangled while you claim e5 and launch a kingside storm.
Against 3...c5, stabilize with 4. e3 first so ...Qa5+ never wins tempo against your knight.
goldenRules: Always check for the ...Qa5+ check before jumping Nb5!
If Black defends c7 with ...Na6, retreat gracefully when kicked—you forced their knight onto the rim.
Once the queenside stabilizes, plant a knight on e5 or castle queenside and throw g4–h4.

lines.title: The c7 Fork Probe (4. Nb5)
lines.subtitle: Punish natural 3...e6 development by dragging Black's knight to the rim
lines.frequencyNote: Catches over 50% of 1000–1500 opponents off guard immediately

annotations.plan: Jump Nb5 immediately! Together with your f4 bishop, you threaten Nxc7+ forking Black's king and rook—forcing awkward concessions.
annotations.cosmicCue: Locking tractor beam on c7.

annotations.plan: Retreat cleanly to c3. Mission accomplished: Black wasted two moves (...Na6 and ...c6) and trapped their light-squared bishop while you develop smoothly.

lines.title: Handling 3...c5 Without Falling for ...Qa5+
lines.subtitle: Keep the center ironclad before jumping into e5
lines.frequencyNote: Black's #1 most critical test against the Jobava

annotations.plan: Play e3 FIRST! Do not jump Nb5 yet—because Black already moved the c-pawn, ...Qa5+ would fork your king and b5 knight.
annotations.cosmicCue: Shields up before warping—watch the a5 diagonal.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: After ...c5, jumping Nb5 immediately runs straight into ...Qa5+! Black chases your knight back and blows up your d4 center.

annotations.plan: Plant Ne5! With your center rock-solid and Black spending a tempo on ...a6, your knight dominates the board and kicks off a strong kingside attack.

counterGuide.title: Anti-Nb5 Shield (...a6 + ...c5)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Play 3...a6! to kill White's Nb5-c7 fork threats cold, then strike the center with ...c5 and ...Nc6.

counterGuide.title: Symmetrical ...Bf5 + ...e6
counterGuide.keyIdea: Develop the c8 bishop early with ...Bf5 and create luft with ...h6 so White's g4-h4 storm bounces off.

name: Italian Game
tagline: Classical 1.e4 development targeting f7 with rapid castling and sharp central breaks.

corePlans: Target Black's weakest square f7 immediately with Bc4 and prepare c3 + d4 to seize the center.
Against 3...Nf6, strike aggressively with 4. Ng5 to test Black's Two Knights Defense immediately.
In quiet Giuoco Pianissimo lines, reroute Nbd2-f1-g3 to aim all pieces at Black's kingside.
goldenRules: Always prepare d4 with c3 first—jumping 4. d4 too early allows clean trades.
Keep the c4 bishop alive via Bb3 if Black pushes ...a6 and ...Na5.
Castle kingside early so Re1 can support an eventual d4 center break.

lines.title: Giuoco Piano: c3 & d4 Center Break
lines.subtitle: Classic rapid center seizure against 3...Bc5
lines.frequencyNote: Most common 1.e4 e5 club battleground

annotations.plan: Play c3 to support a full d4 central push while building a b3 retreat square for your bishop.
annotations.cosmicCue: Charge the central thruster before firing d4.

annotations.plan: Recapture cxd4! Now you have a massive d4+e4 pawn center attacking Black's c5 bishop with tempo.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Recapturing with the knight leaves e4 undefended—Black grabs a free central pawn with ...Nxe4!

lines.title: Two Knights: 4. Ng5 Fried Liver Probe

annotations.cosmicCue: Lock onto the f7 reactor immediately.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Grabbing e5 hangs your knight cleanly and lets Black win your c4 bishop too!

annotations.plan: Deliver Bb5+ with tempo! After 6...c6 7. dxc6 bxc6 8. Be2, you stay a clean pawn up with a solid kingside.

lines.subtitle: Claim a commanding center against Black's passive bishop

annotations.plan: Strike the center immediately with d4! Because Black's bishop is passive on e7, you don't need c3 first.
Push d5 to kick the c6 knight all the way back to b8 and follow up with c4 for a massive space edge.

counterGuide.title: Two Knights Counter-Attack (3...Nf6)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Meet 3.Bc4 with 3...Nf6!; against 4.Ng5, sacrifice a pawn with 4...d5 5.exd5 Na5! for blazing piece activity.

counterGuide.title: Solid Giuoco Piano (...Bc5 + ...a6 + ...Ba7)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Tuck the c5 bishop safely on a7 so White's d4 push never wins a tempo, then fight evenly in the center.

name: Queen's Gambit (QGD & QGA)
tagline: Complete White 1.d4 + 2.c4 repertoire covering QGD, QGA, Slav & the famous ...b5/...c6 6.Qf3! refutation.

corePlans: Attack Black's d5 anchor immediately with 2. c4 to deflect it from the center.
Against QGA (2...dxc4), punish greedy 3. e3 b5? 4. a4 c6? with 5. axb5 cxb5 6. Qf3!! skewering the a8 rook.
Against QGD (2...e6), play either the Exchange Minority Attack (4. cxd5 + 5. Bg5) or the Classical 4. Bg5 squeeze.
goldenRules: Develop Bg5 BEFORE playing e3 in the QGD Exchange so your dark-squared bishop never gets trapped.
Never fear 2...dxc4 — if Black clings to c4 with ...b5 and ...c6, 4. a4 + 5. axb5 + 6. Qf3!! wins a piece or rook.
Against the 2...c6 Slav (...dxc4), play 5. a4 immediately to stop ...b5 cold.

lines.title: QGA ...c6 Refutation: 3. e3 b5? 4. a4 c6? 6. Qf3!
lines.subtitle: Punish greedy QGA players trying to cling to c4 — win a full piece or the a8 rook
lines.frequencyNote: Essential refutation every 1. d4 player wins dozens of games with

annotations.plan: Play 3. e3 to prepare Bxc4 cleanly while opening the d1-h5 diagonal — setting a lethal trap if Black tries to hold c4 with 3...b5?.
annotations.cosmicCue: Bait the greed sensor: leave c4 dangling while your queen locks onto a8.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Early Qa4+ exposes your queen and drops the d4 pawn right away after ...Nc6 Qxc4 Qxd4!

annotations.plan: Strike immediately with 4. a4! You undermine the b5 defender of c4. Note that 4...a6? also loses to 5. axb5 because Black's a6 pawn is pinned to the a8 rook!
annotations.cosmicCue: Fire a4 at the support strut — the entire queenside collapses.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Capturing c4 while b5 defends it drops a full bishop! Always undermine b5 with 4. a4 first.

annotations.plan: Black played 4...c6? to reinforce b5 — rip open the long diagonal with 5. axb5! Now after 5...cxb5, the a8 rook has zero protection.
annotations.cosmicCue: Clear the laser corridor from h1 straight into a8.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Developing quietly with 5. Nc3? lets Black push ...b4 with tempo and keep the extra pawn — trade immediately with 5. axb5!

annotations.plan: 6. Qf3!! — THE FAMOUS ...c6 REFUTATION! You skewer the trapped a8 rook down the wide-open diagonal. Black must drop a full knight (6...Nc6 7. Qxc6+) or lose the rook (6...Nd7 7. Qxa8 / 6...Bb7 7. Qxb7).
annotations.cosmicCue: Direct tractor-beam hit on a8! Black drops a clean piece by force.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing 6. b3? misses the winning 6. Qf3!! skewer and gives Black time to plug the diagonal with ...Bb7!

annotations.plan: Snap off the knight with check! 7. Qxc6+ leaves you up a clean piece with total control.
Retreat cleanly to f3 up a full knight, keeping pressure on the queenside while you develop Nc3, Nge2, and castle.

lines.subtitle: Punish 2...dxc4 by taking full central control

annotations.plan: Grab the center with 3. e4! You immediately threaten Bxc4 and dominate both central squares.

annotations.plan: Regain the c4 pawn cleanly with tempo on the d5 knight while keeping a towering e5 space wedge.

Play 7. Qe2! This clears d1 for your rook, dodges an early queen trade, and sets up Rd1 x-raying Black's queen.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Trading on c5 too early swaps queens and develops Black's bishop for free — keep the tension with 7. Qe2!

annotations.plan: Centralize with 9. Rd1! Your rook x-rays Black's d8 queen so upcoming e4 or d5 breaks pack serious tactical punch.

lines.subtitle: Structured, easy-to-play Carlsbad middlegame plans against 2...e6

annotations.plan: Capture 4. cxd5 to lock in the Carlsbad pawn structure — this opens your c-file and sets up the classic b2-b4-b5 minority attack.
Pin the f6 knight with Bg5 BEFORE playing e3! Your dark-squared bishop stays active outside the pawn chain.
annotations.cosmicCue: Deploy the bishop outside before closing the blast doors.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing e3 first entombs your c1 bishop—always put Bg5 on the board before e3!

annotations.plan: Put Qc2 on the b1-h7 diagonal to eye h7 and discourage Black's ...Bf5.

annotations.plan: Pin the defender of d5 immediately with 4. Bg5! Keep the c4-d5 tension alive while developing smoothly.
Retreat 7. Bh4! Preserve the pin on the f6 knight — never surrender your bishop pair without a concrete reason.
annotations.cosmicCue: Hold the magnetic pin on h4 — make Black weaken their kingside.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Giving up Bxf6 for nothing hands Black the bishop pair and solves their cramped position — keep the pin with 7. Bh4!

annotations.plan: Strike 8. cxd5 right after Black plays ...b6! This forces hanging or backward queenside pawns and opens the c-file for your rook.
Seize the half-open c-file immediately with 11. Rc1! Black's c7 and d5 pawns are long-term targets for Be2, O-O, and Qa4.

lines.title: Slav Defense (2...c6): Stop ...b5 with 5. a4
lines.subtitle: Prevent Black from clinging to the c4 pawn in the 2...c6 Slav

counterGuide.title: Queen's Gambit Declined (2...e6)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Hold d5 like granite with ...e6 and ...Nf6, break the pin with ...Be7 + ...h6, and equalize with ...b6 and ...c5.

counterGuide.title: Queen's Gambit Accepted (2...dxc4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Capture c4 to pull White's bishop off the f1-a6 diagonal, then counter-strike immediately with ...c5 and ...a6/...b5 — never fall for 3...b5 4. a4 c6? 6. Qf3!.

name: Accelerated Dragon Sicilian
tagline: Sharp 1...c5 counterattack with a razor-sharp g7 dragon bishop and low-theory setups.

corePlans: Fianchetto the dark-squared bishop on g7 to slice across the entire h8-a1 diagonal.
Keep your d-pawn on d7 initially so you can smash the center with ...d5 in ONE move when ready.
Use the half-open c-file with ...Rc8 and target White's c3 knight and e4 pawn.
goldenRules: Play 4...g6 BEFORE ...d6 to sidestep the fierce Yugoslav Attack.
Against the Alapin (2. c3), immediately hit back with 2...d5!
Against the Bowdler Attack (2. Bc4), blunt the bishop with ...e6 and strike with ...d5.

lines.title: Open Sicilian: Accelerated Dragon Mainline

annotations.plan: Fianchetto immediately with 4...g6! Your bishop will soon snipe the d4 knight and the entire long diagonal.

Unleash ...d5! You hit the c4 bishop with tempo and claim a broad, comfortable center.

counterGuide.title: Maroczy Bind (5.c4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Clamp down on d5 forever with 5.c4! — the Maroczy Bind robs Black of the ...d5 break and gives White a lasting space grip.

counterGuide.title: Rossolimo Sideline (3.Bb5)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Avoid Black's Dragon theory completely by pinning c6 on move 3 and playing for a clean positional squeeze.

name: French Defense
tagline: Rock-solid 1...e6 counterpuncher—undermine White's d4 pawn chain with ...c5 and ...Qb6.

corePlans: Always attack the base of White's d4-e5 pawn chain with ...c5 BEFORE developing the b8 knight.
Pile onto d4 and b2 simultaneously with ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 (often backed by ...Nh6-f5).
If White plays the Exchange (3. exd5 exd5), develop smoothly with ...Bd6, ...Ne7, ...O-O, and ...Bf5.
goldenRules: Golden Rule #1 of the French: play ...c5 BEFORE ...Nc6—never block your own c-pawn!
Look for ...f6 later to demolish White's e5 spearhead once your pieces are ready.
Don't panic about your c8 bishop—trade it off via ...Bd7-b5 or activate it after ...f6.

lines.title: Advance French: Destroy d4 with ...c5 & ...Qb6
lines.subtitle: Relentless pawn-chain counterattack against 3. e5
lines.frequencyNote: White's #1 choice against the French at club level

annotations.plan: Immediately hit the base of White's pawn chain with 3...c5! Never put Nc6 in front of your c-pawn.
annotations.cosmicCue: Strike the hull base at d4 before anything else.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing 3...Nc6? blocks your vital ...c5 pawn break and leaves you cramped with zero pressure on d4!

annotations.plan: Swing ...Qb6 to double up on d4 and hit b2—this pins White's dark-squared bishop to defending b2.

lines.title: Classical French (3. Nc3 Nf6): Steinitz Counterattack
lines.subtitle: Provoke 4. e5 and immediately smash the center with ...c5
lines.frequencyNote: Main theoretical test against 1...e6

annotations.plan: Retreat 4...Nfd7! From d7 your knight supports both ...c5 and ...f6 breaks and keeps f6 clear for counterplay.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Retreating all the way back to g8 wastes two tempi and gives White a free attack.

annotations.plan: Smash the center with 5...c5! Now White's overextended d4-e5-f4 chain comes under heavy fire.

lines.title: Exchange French (3. exd5): Active ...Bd6 & ...Bf5
lines.subtitle: Never fall asleep in the Exchange—develop actively and claim equality
lines.frequencyNote: Popular solid choice by White players trying to avoid theory

annotations.plan: Place 4...Bd6 on the active b8-h2 diagonal and pair it with ...Ne7 and ...Bf5 to neutralize White's light-squared bishop.
Play ...Bf5! Trading off White's strong d3 bishop leaves you with effortless equality and a nice outpost on f5.

counterGuide.title: Tarrasch System (3.Nd2)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Avoid the Winawer ...Bb4 pin with 3.Nd2, keep flexible c3 support, and punish Black's exposed queen after ...c5.

counterGuide.title: Advance Space Clamp (3.e5 + c3)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Lock in a kingside space edge with 3.e5, reinforce d4 with c3, and build a kingside attack while Black's c8 bishop sits trapped.

name: The Alien Gambit
tagline: BrillyDer’s signature knight sacrifice on f7 vs the Caro-Kann — rip the Black king into open space.

corePlans: Lure 5...h6 with 5. Ng5, then detonate 6. Nxf7! Kxf7 to drag the Black king into the center and destroy castling rights.
Plant a monster knight on e5 (Nf3-e5+) and aim Bc4+ right down the a2-g8 diagonal.
Keep every piece racing forward (O-O, Re1, Qe2) — Black’s extra piece is useless while their king is trapped in the middle.
goldenRules: Never trade queens while down a piece — keep attacking fuel on the board.
Control e5 and the a2-g8 diagonal before Black can consolidate with ...Kg8 and ...e6.
If Black avoids 5...h6 with 5...Bf5, pivot smoothly into a dominant Ne5 kingside clamp.

lines.title: Main Line vs 7...Bf5
lines.subtitle: Shatter the shelter with 6. Nxf7! and lock down the e5 outpost
lines.frequencyNote: Most common club defense after 6. Nxf7 Kxf7 7. Nf3

annotations.plan: Play 5. Ng5! Instead of retreating or trading on f6, you bait 5...h6 to launch the Alien Gambit.
annotations.cosmicCue: Bait the shield wall — charge the f7 warp core.

annotations.plan: 6. Nxf7!! The signature Alien Gambit sacrifice. Black’s king is forced to f7, losing castling rights and exposing the e5 and c4 squares.
annotations.cosmicCue: Detonate on f7! Drag the enemy flagship out of dock.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Retreating with 6. N5f3 wastes a tempo and lets Black develop comfortably with ...Bg4 and ...e6.

annotations.plan: Jump immediately into e5 with check! 8. Ne5+ drives the king back to e8 and blocks Black’s e-pawn.
annotations.cosmicCue: Lock onto the e5 beacon with check.

annotations.plan: Develop 9. Bc4 targeting the weak e6/f7 complex, followed by O-O and Qe2/Re1 for a crushing initiative.
annotations.cosmicCue: Sweep the a2-g8 laser across the stranded king.

lines.title: Dark-Square Siege vs 7...e6
lines.subtitle: Aim Bd3 + Ne5+ at g6 when Black tries to tuck the king away
lines.frequencyNote: Popular practical attempt to return to safety via ...Kg8

annotations.plan: Against 7...e6, place the bishop on d3 instead of c4 — it targets the newly weakened g6 square and h7.
annotations.cosmicCue: Target the g6 hull breach.

annotations.plan: 11. Ng6! Forking the h8 rook and cementing a monster outpost on the kingside.
annotations.cosmicCue: Board the enemy reactor on g6.

lines.title: Declined: 5...Bf5
lines.subtitle: Claim a huge positional edge when Black refuses to play ...h6
lines.frequencyNote: How stronger Caro-Kann players try to sidestep 6. Nxf7

annotations.plan: 7. Ne5! Threatening both Ngxf7 and Nxg6. Black is forced to tuck the bishop back to g6.
annotations.cosmicCue: Double-threaten f7 and g6 in one leap.

annotations.plan: Push 8. h4! Threatening h5 to trap or dismantle the g6 bishop and grab the bishop pair.
annotations.cosmicCue: Launch the h-pawn battering ram.

counterGuide.title: Cool-Headed Acceptance + ...Be6
counterGuide.keyIdea: Accept the knight on f7, cover e5 with ...Be6, tuck your king safely on g8, and enjoy being a clean piece up!

counterGuide.title: Sidestep Early with 4...Bf5
counterGuide.keyIdea: Play the Classical 4...Bf5 instead of 4...Nf6 — the Alien Gambit 5.Ng5 is completely impossible against Bf5.

name: Vienna Gambit
tagline: Blast open the f-file with 3. f4 and overrun unprepared 1...e5 players.

corePlans: If Black greedily takes 3...exf4, unleash 4. e5! kicking the f6 knight all the way back to g8 and seizing the whole center.
Against the best defense 3...d5, play 4. fxe5 Nxe4 5. Nf3 and build a towering d4 + Bd3 + O-O kingside attack.
Use the open f-file after O-O to pile up rooks and pieces on f7.
goldenRules: Always meet 3...exf4 with 4. e5! — never allow Black to keep the f6 knight active.
Keep d4 protected before pushing e5 unless Black’s knight has no safe forward squares.
Castle kingside early so your f1 rook immediately owns the half-open f-file.

lines.title: Accepted 3...exf4 — Center Stampede
lines.subtitle: Kick the knight back to g8 and crush Black’s cramped position
lines.frequencyNote: Over 50% of club players fall into 3...exf4?

annotations.plan: 3. f4! The Vienna Gambit. You challenge e5 immediately while keeping the f1-a6 diagonal and f-file ready.
annotations.cosmicCue: Ignite the f4 solar flare.

annotations.plan: 4. e5! The knight has zero safe forward squares (Qe7 is met by Qe2) and must retreat in shame to g8.
annotations.cosmicCue: Send the knight back to orbit on g8.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Delaying e5 lets Black strike back with 4...d5 and equalize effortlessly.

annotations.plan: 7. Qe2 pins the e5 pawn to the king and prepares Bxf4 + O-O-O or O-O with a huge lead in development.
annotations.cosmicCue: Pin the e-file and mobilize every thruster.

lines.title: Main Line 3...d5 Counter-Strike
lines.subtitle: Solidify with Nf3 + d4 + Bd3 and attack down the open f-file
lines.frequencyNote: Black’s strongest theoretical reply to 3. f4

annotations.plan: 4. fxe5 opens the f-file for your rook while forcing Black’s knight onto e4.
annotations.cosmicCue: Crack open the f-file corridor.

annotations.plan: 7. Bd3 challenges the e4 knight and aims straight at h7 once Black castles.
annotations.cosmicCue: Lock the bishop onto e4 and h7.

annotations.plan: Capture en passant (8. exf6) to keep the e-file and f-file wide open for your pieces.
annotations.cosmicCue: Clear the lane with en passant.

lines.title: Passive 3...Nc6 — Classic f-File Crush
lines.subtitle: Win massive space with fxe5, d4, and e5
lines.frequencyNote: Very common below 1600 when Black develops instinctively

annotations.plan: 5. d4! Kick the e5 knight immediately and build a colossal pawn duo.
annotations.cosmicCue: Claim the entire center with tempo.

annotations.plan: 6. e5! Once again the f6 knight is driven all the way back to g8.
annotations.cosmicCue: Push Black’s pieces off the board.

counterGuide.title: Central Counter-Strike (3...d5!)
counterGuide.keyIdea: NEVER take 3...exf4? — immediately strike the center with 3...d5! to equalize effortlessly and keep an active knight on e4.

counterGuide.title: Declined with 2...Nc6
counterGuide.keyIdea: Meet 2.Nc3 with 2...Nc6 so White's f4 gambit loses its sting against your rock-solid central control.

name: Stafford Gambit
tagline: Sacrifice a pawn on move 3 to unleash lethal ...Bc5, ...Ng4, and ...Qh4 mating webs.

corePlans: Always recapture 4...dxc6! opening BOTH the c8 bishop and the d8 queen on move 4.
Aim ...Bc5 at f2, launch ...h5 to protect ...Ng4, and swing the queen to d6 or h4 for unstoppable mating threats.
Watch for the famous ...Nxe4! queen-sacrifice trap whenever White plays Bg5.
goldenRules: Never recapture 4...bxc6 — 4...dxc6 is the entire point of the Stafford Gambit.
If White plays Bg5 while f2 is undefended, check if ...Nxe4! wins immediately.
In blitz & rapid, prioritize piece speed and open lines over winning back the pawn.

lines.title: The Classic 6. Bg5 ...Nxe4! Mate Trap
lines.subtitle: Sacrifice the queen on d8 to deliver a stunning 8...Bg4# checkmate
lines.frequencyNote: One of the most famous traps in online chess history

annotations.plan: 4...dxc6! Opens both diagonals for your queen and c8 bishop for instant piece activity.
annotations.cosmicCue: Unleash the queen and bishop in one capture.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: 4...bxc6 keeps your queen and c8 bishop locked in — you lose all the Stafford traps.

annotations.plan: 6...Nxe4!! Ignoring the pin on your queen! If White takes on d8, 7...Bxf2+ 8. Ke2 Bg4# is pure checkmate.
annotations.cosmicCue: Oh no, my queen! Spring the Legall-style mate.

annotations.plan: 8...Bg4# Checkmate! Both bishops and the e4 knight weave a flawless mating net.
annotations.cosmicCue: Target neutralized — checkmate in 8.

lines.title: Against 5. e5 — The ...Ne4 & ...Bxf2+ Strike
lines.subtitle: Punish greedy 6. d3? or 7. dxe4? with a crushing tactic on f2
lines.frequencyNote: Frequent knee-jerk reaction from 1. e4 players

annotations.plan: 5...Ne4! Centralize aggressively instead of retreating — you already eye f2 and c5.
annotations.cosmicCue: Dive into e4 and paint a target on f2.

annotations.plan: 6...Bc5! Leaving the e4 knight as bait. Taking it walks straight into 7...Bxf2+ winning the d1 queen!
annotations.cosmicCue: Leave the knight as venom bait.

annotations.plan: 8...Bg4+! Skewers the king and wins White’s queen on d1 cleanly.
annotations.cosmicCue: Skewer the flagship on d1.

lines.title: Solid 6. Be2 — The ...h5 & ...Ng4 Storm
lines.subtitle: Launch a full-scale kingside assault with ...h5, ...Ng4, and ...Qd6
lines.frequencyNote: Main battleground when White plays solidly with Be2 + O-O

annotations.plan: 6...h5! Prepares ...Ng4 (making Bxg4 hxg4 open the h-file for your rook).
annotations.cosmicCue: Anchor the g4 launchpad and prime the h-file.

annotations.plan: 8...Qd6! Threatening ...Qh2# mate! If White plays hxg4, ...hxg4 unleashes a devastating h-file attack.
annotations.cosmicCue: Point the queen straight at h2.

counterGuide.title: The f3 + d4 Refutation Wall
counterGuide.keyIdea: Play 5.d3! and 6.Be2! (never Bg5? or Bc4? into ...Ng4 tricks!), calmly shutting down every Stafford trap a clean pawn up.

counterGuide.title: Nc3 + Be3 Anti-Trap Setup
counterGuide.keyIdea: Play h3 early to forbid ...Ng4 completely, castle safely, and convert your extra central pawn in the endgame.

name: Englund Gambit
tagline: Ambush 1. d4 players immediately with 1...e5 and weaponize ...Qb4+ double-attack traps.

corePlans: Throw 1. d4 London players completely out of their comfort zone on move 1 with 1...e5!
Pair 2...Nc6 and 3...Qe7 to attack e5 and set up the lethal ...Qb4+ double attack against b2 and f4.
Pin the c3 bishop with ...Bb4 and race into White’s back rank on c1.
goldenRules: Against 4. Bf4, ALWAYS check with 4...Qb4+ — it forks the king, the f4 bishop, and the b2 pawn.
After 5. Bd2 Qxb2 6. Bc3, unleash 6...Bb4! pinning the bishop to the queen and rook.
If White avoids the trap with 6. Nc3, pin with 6...Bb4 and fight for rapid piece activity.

lines.title: The Famous 4. Bf4 Qb4+ Mate Trap
lines.subtitle: Pin with 6...Bb4 and deliver 8...Qc1# back-rank checkmate
lines.frequencyNote: Catches thousands of London System players off guard

annotations.plan: 3...Qe7! Attacks e5 a second time and sets up the deadly ...Qb4+ fork against any London-style 4. Bf4.
annotations.cosmicCue: Prime the Qb4+ ambush.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Developing 3...Bc5 before ...Qe7 lets White keep the extra pawn comfortably with Qd5 or Bf4.

annotations.plan: 4...Qb4+! Triple-forking the king, the f4 bishop, and the b2 pawn.
annotations.cosmicCue: Triple fork! King, bishop, and b2 all under fire.

annotations.plan: 6...Bb4!! Pins the c3 bishop to the queen and a1 rook. If White plays 7. Qd2 Bxc3 8. Qxc3, 8...Qc1# is instant checkmate!
annotations.cosmicCue: Pin the c3 defender and lock the c1 hatch.

annotations.plan: 8...Qc1# Checkmate! The back rank collapses in 8 moves.
annotations.cosmicCue: Warp complete — back-rank checkmate!

lines.title: Against 6. Nc3 — The ...Bb4 Pin
lines.subtitle: Keep the initiative alive when White sidesteps 6. Bc3
lines.frequencyNote: Best practical reply for White after 5...Qxb2

annotations.plan: 6...Bb4! Pin the c3 knight immediately so White cannot easily trap your queen.
annotations.cosmicCue: Pin the knight before retreating the queen.

annotations.plan: 8...Qa5 keeps pressure on e5 and c3 while preparing ...Nge7 and ...O-O.
annotations.cosmicCue: Sidestep the rook and maintain full fire on c3.

lines.title: Against 4. Qd5 — Rapid ...f6 Gambit
lines.subtitle: Open the f-file and gain huge development tempos on White’s queen

annotations.plan: 4...f6! Offer a second pawn to open the f-file and kick the White queen around with ...Nxf6.
annotations.cosmicCue: Feed a second pawn for hyperdrive development.

annotations.plan: 6...d5 claims the center and opens your c8 bishop for ...Be6 and ...O-O-O.
annotations.cosmicCue: Seize the center while White’s pieces sleep.

counterGuide.title: Refuting the Queen Raid (5.Nc3!)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Do NOT fall for 6.Qd2? Bb4! — instead play 6.Bd2! Qxb2 7.Nc3! and trap/harass Black's queen with Rb1 and Nd5 for a winning attack.

counterGuide.title: Clean Development (4.Qd5 / 5.e4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Skip all the ...Qb4+ b2 complications by playing 4.Nc3! — even if Black regains the pawn, White has a massive lead in development.

name: Ruy Lopez
tagline: The classical king of 1.e4 openings — pressure e5, castle fast, and dominate the center with c3 + d4.

corePlans: Build a rock-solid center with c3 and d4 while Re1 defends e4.
Reroute the queenside knight via Nbd2-f1-g3 (the classic Ruy Lopez maneuver) to attack the kingside.
Keep the Spanish bishop alive on b3/c2 aiming straight at f7.
goldenRules: Do not rush Bxc6 unless you want the structural Exchange endgame — keeping the light-squared bishop fuels your kingside attack.
Play h3 before d4 if Black threatens ...Bg4 pinning your f3 knight.

lines.title: Closed Morphy Defense (c3 + d4)
lines.subtitle: The timeless main line — castle, fortify e4, and launch d4.
lines.frequencyNote: Most common club & master response

annotations.plan: Bb5 pressures the c6 defender of e5 and prepares rapid kingside castling.
Re1 overprotects e4 so White now genuinely threatens Bxc6 followed by Nxe5.
c3 carves out the c2 retreat for the Spanish bishop and prepares d4.
d4 strikes the center with full support — White enjoys space and a classic kingside plan.

lines.title: Anti-Berlin (4.d3)
lines.subtitle: Sidestep the dry Berlin endgame and keep a rich middlegame fight.
lines.frequencyNote: Popular against 3...Nf6

annotations.plan: d3 calmly defends e4, keeping queens on the board and avoiding the Berlin Wall endgame.
c3 prepares d4 later and gives the b5 bishop a safe home.
h3 prevents ...Bg4 and readies Nbd2-f1-g3.

lines.title: Exchange Variation (4.Bxc6)
lines.subtitle: Damage Black's pawn structure early and play for a clean king-and-pawn edge.
lines.frequencyNote: Practical weapon vs 3...a6

annotations.plan: Bxc6 doubles Black's c-pawns; White's 4-vs-3 kingside pawn majority wins almost every pure pawn endgame.
d4 opens the center immediately while Black's king is still uncastled.

counterGuide.title: Berlin Defense (3...Nf6)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Trade queens early into the legendary Berlin Wall — Black's bishop pair and rock-solid structure neutralize White's attack.

counterGuide.title: Open Spanish Counter-Attack (5...Nxe4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Grab e4 on move 5 instead of defending passively — Black seizes active piece play on the queenside and open center.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
tagline: Ultra-solid yet counter-punching defense to 1.e4 — develop the c8 bishop outside the pawn chain and strike with ...c5.

corePlans: Activate your light-squared bishop (Bf5 or Bg4) BEFORE locking the center with ...e6.
Undermine White's space advantage with timely ...c5 breaks.
Trade into endgames where your clean pawn structure shines.
goldenRules: After 3.e5 Bf5, remember ...h6 or ...h5 to give your bishop an escape square on h7.
In the Classical 4...Bf5, play ...Nd7 before ...Ngf6 to avoid doubled f-pawns.

lines.title: Classical Main Line (4...Bf5)
lines.subtitle: Activate the light-squared bishop cleanly and build an unbreakable fortress.
lines.frequencyNote: Gold standard vs 3.Nc3

annotations.plan: Bf5 claims the h7-b1 diagonal before closing the e6 door.
h6 creates the vital h7 sanctuary for the bishop against h5.
Nd7 develops harmoniously and guards f6.

lines.title: Advance Variation (3...Bf5 + ...c5)
lines.subtitle: Get the bishop out, then blow up White's d4-e5 pawn chain with ...c5.
lines.frequencyNote: Most frequent club line

annotations.plan: Bf5 solves Black's bad-bishop problem immediately.
...c5 attacks the base of White's d4-e5 chain at once.

lines.title: Exchange Variation (3.exd5 cxd5)
lines.subtitle: Enjoy the open c-file and launch a textbook queenside minority attack.
lines.frequencyNote: Common quiet White choice

annotations.plan: Nc6 immediately eyes d4 and develops rapidly.
Bg4 activates the bishop outside the pawn chain before playing ...e6.

counterGuide.title: Tal Variation (3.e5 Bf5 4.h4!)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Hit Black's f5 bishop immediately with 4.h4! to provoke a weakening ...h5 or ...h6 and seize dark-square control.

counterGuide.title: Two Knights Attack (2.Nc3 + 3.Nf3)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Sidestep main Caro-Kann theory, grab the bishop pair after ...Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3, and launch a fast kingside initiative.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined (QGD)
tagline: The ultimate classical defense to 1.d4 — hold d5 with ...e6, castle safely, and equalize cleanly with ...c5 or ...e5.

corePlans: Anchor your d5 stronghold with ...e6 and ...Nf6 so White never gets a free e4 steamroller.
Break the Bg5 pin early with ...Be7, ...O-O, and ...h6.
Free the c8 bishop via ...b6 + ...Bb7 (Tartakower) or ...dxc4 followed by ...c5.
goldenRules: Never panic about the c8 bishop — once you play ...c5 or ...b6 + ...Bb7 it becomes your best piece.
Against the Exchange QGD (cxd5 exd5), remember ...c6 + ...Bf5/Be7 + ...Nd7 before castling.

lines.title: Tartakower Defense (...h6 & ...b6)
lines.subtitle: World Champion favorite — fianchetto the c8 bishop and strike with ...c5.
lines.frequencyNote: Top mainline vs 4.Bg5

annotations.plan: e6 reinforces d5 solidly and opens the f8-a3 diagonal for ...Be7.
h6 questions the g5 bishop and gives the Black king luft.
b6 prepares ...Bb7 and ...c5, fully liberating Black's queenside.

lines.title: Exchange Variation Defense (4.cxd5 exd5)
lines.subtitle: Meet White's minority attack with active piece play on the e-file.
lines.frequencyNote: Most common club try vs QGD

annotations.plan: exd5 instantly opens the c8-h3 diagonal for your light-squared bishop!
c6 cements d5 and prepares ...Nbd7-f8-e6 or ...Re8.

lines.title: Ragozin Counter-Pin (4...Bb4)
lines.subtitle: Dynamic modern QGD — pin c3 immediately and fight for active piece play.
lines.frequencyNote: Super-GM sharp weapon

annotations.plan: Bb4 pins the c3 knight and threatens ...dxc4 with active counterplay.
dxc4 grabs the pawn only once White's bishop is committed to h4.

counterGuide.title: Exchange QGD Minority Attack (b4-b5)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Clarify the center early with cxd5, then push Rb1 + b4-b5 to shatter Black's c6-d5 pawns and create a weak backward c6 pawn.

counterGuide.title: Catalan Squeeze (g3 + Bg2)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Fianchetto on g2 to exert relentless long-diagonal pressure across Black's entire queenside.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted (QGA)
tagline: Take the c4 pawn, give it back on your terms, and strike White's center with ...c5 and rapid piece development.

corePlans: Do NOT try to cling to the c4 pawn with ...b5? — use White's time recovering it to seize active development.
Strike the center immediately with ...c5 and gain queenside space with ...a6 + ...b5 + ...Bb7.
Enjoy completely open diagonals for both bishops with zero cramped QGD pieces.
goldenRules: If White plays 3.e4, immediately hit back with 3...e5! or 3...Nf6 — never let White keep a free d4+e4 center.
Watch out for the classic trap 3.e3 b5? 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5 6.Qf3! winning the a8 rook.

lines.title: Classical Main Line (3.Nf3 Nf6 4.e3 e6 5.Bxc4 c5)
lines.subtitle: Clean, active equality with fast queenside expansion (...a6, ...b5, ...Bb7).
lines.frequencyNote: Main theoretical battleground

annotations.plan: dxc4 surrenders the d5 point temporarily to open lines and hit White with ...c5.
...c5 challenges d4 immediately while White's bishop just spent a tempo recapturing.
...b5 gains tempo on the c4 bishop and prepares ...Bb7.

lines.title: Countering 3.e4 with 3...e5!
lines.subtitle: Punish White's greedy 3.e4 center immediately by blowing open the d-file.
lines.frequencyNote: Most aggressive White try

annotations.plan: 3...e5! directly undermines White's d4 pawn — if 4.dxe5 Qxd1+ 5.Kxd1 Black is completely fine.
Be6 neutralizes White's dangerous c4 bishop cleanly.

lines.title: Countering 3.e3 with 3...e5!
lines.subtitle: Instantly free your c8 bishop and seize active central play.
lines.frequencyNote: Common club shortcut

annotations.plan: 3...e5! takes advantage of 3.e3 not controlling e5 — Black equalizes effortlessly.
Bb4+ develops with tempo and prepares rapid castling.

counterGuide.title: Central Steamroller (3.e4)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Claim both central squares with 3.e4! immediately — if Black doesn't counter with 3...e5!, White builds a huge space advantage.

counterGuide.title: Mannheim Queen Check (3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Qa4+)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Recover the c4 pawn cleanly while disrupting Black's queenside development with 4.Qa4+.

name: Scotch Game
tagline: Blast open the 1.e4 e5 center on move 3 — clean tactical play, Mieses space squeeze & Scotch Gambit blitz.

corePlans: Strike immediately with 3. d4 to avoid long closed Ruy Lopez/Italian maneuvering.
Against 4...Nf6, double Black's pawns with 5. Nxc6 bxc6 and seize space with 6. e5!.
Against 4...Bc5, hold d4 solidly with 5. Be3 + 6. c3 before developing Bc4 and castling.
goldenRules: In the Mieses (4...Nf6), play 5. Nxc6 BEFORE pushing e5 so Black's knight is forced to awkward squares.
Against 4...Bc5, play 5. Be3 first — never trade 5. Nxc6? into 5...Qf6!.
In the 4. Bc4 Scotch Gambit, always meet 4...Nf6 with 5. e5! to seize the initiative.

lines.title: Mieses Variation: 4...Nf6 5. Nxc6 & 6. e5!
lines.subtitle: Kasparov's favorite weapon — wreck Black's structure and claim space
lines.frequencyNote: Most popular Black response to the Scotch at 1200–2200 Elo

annotations.plan: Open the center immediately with 3. d4! Black must surrender the e5 anchor with 3...exd4.
annotations.cosmicCue: Detonate the center on move 3 before Black can build shields.

annotations.plan: Trade 5. Nxc6! Wreck Black's queenside pawn structure first so 6. e5! drives the f6 knight into an awkward pin.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Allowing 5...Bb4 pins your knight and lets Black attack e4 before you seize space with 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. e5!.

annotations.plan: Push 6. e5! Immediately kick the knight while Black's d-pawn is still stuck on d7.
Claim even more central territory with 8. c4! Push the d5 knight back and lock down the board.

lines.title: Classical 4...Bc5: 5. Be3 & Solid c3 Fortress
lines.subtitle: Neutralize Black's f2 pressure and launch a clean kingside initiative
lines.frequencyNote: Very common at club level against the Scotch

annotations.plan: Defend d4 actively with 5. Be3! You develop with tempo and threaten Nxc6 + Bxc5.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Trading on c6 lets Black jump into f6 with a mate threat on f2 and free development — play 5. Be3! first.

annotations.plan: Reinforce d4 like granite with 6. c3! Now Black's queen and bishop bounce right off your center.
Castle calmly with 9. O-O! Don't fear 9...Qxe4? — your lead in development and Nd2 crush the greedy queen.

lines.title: Scotch Gambit (4. Bc4): Rapid Development Blitz
lines.subtitle: Skip recapturing d4 immediately and target f7 with blistering tempo
lines.frequencyNote: Sharp tactical alternative that crushes unprepared 1...e5 players

annotations.plan: Aim straight at f7 with 4. Bc4! Instead of recapturing d4 right away, you race ahead in development.
Strike with 5. e5! Drive the knight forward and meet 5...d5 with the sharp 6. Bb5! pin.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Recapturing on d4 drops your e4 pawn immediately to 5...Nxe4! — always push 5. e5! first.

annotations.plan: Regain the d4 pawn cleanly while keeping a crushing pin against Black's c6 knight.

counterGuide.title: 4...Nf6 (Schmidt Counterattack)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Counter-attack e4 immediately with 4...Nf6; after 5. Nxc6 bxc6 6. e5, pin the pawn with 6...Qe7 and centralize on d5.

counterGuide.title: 4...Bc5 (Classical Pressure)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Develop swiftly with 4...Bc5 and 5...Qf6 to pile pressure onto d4 and prepare a quick ...d5 break.

name: English Opening
tagline: Strategic 1.c4 flank mastery — Reversed Sicilian Dragon, Symmetrical d4 breaks & the Botvinnik Triangle.

corePlans: Control d5 from the flank with 1. c4 and unleash a monster fianchettoed Bg2 down the h1-a8 diagonal.
Against 1...e5, play a Reversed Sicilian with an extra tempo — trade cxd5 whenever Black plays ...d5.
Use the Botvinnik Triangle (c4 + d3 + e4 + Nge2) to lock down d5 and launch a kingside f4 storm.
goldenRules: In the Reversed Sicilian, always trade cxd5 when Black pushes ...d5 so you keep an extra central pawn.

annotations.plan: Always capture 4. cxd5! Trade your wing c-pawn for Black's central d-pawn and expose the d5 knight to Bg2.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Skipping 4. cxd5 lets Black grab c4 and equalize comfortably — trade wing pawn for center pawn first!

annotations.plan: Develop 9. Be3 to control d4 and prepare Rc1 + Ne4-c5 queenside domination.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Playing 7. d3 passively lets Black stay completely symmetrical and comfortable — claim the center with 7. d4!.

annotations.plan: Centralize with 9. Qxd4! With Black's c6 knight gone, your queen dominates the center safely.

lines.title: Botvinnik Triangle (c4 + d3 + e4): d5 Outpost

annotations.plan: Lock in the Botvinnik Triangle with 6. e4! You clamp down on d5 permanently while preparing Nge2 + O-O + f4.

annotations.plan: Play 7. Nge2! Keep the f-pawn free for f2-f4 and leave your g2 bishop completely unobstructed.

wrongMoveTraps.reason: Developing 7. Nf3 blocks your f-pawn and hands Black an annoying ...Bg4 pin — always put the knight on e2 in the Botvinnik!

annotations.plan: Plant your knight on the monster 9. Nd5 outpost! Black's pieces are squeezed on both flanks.

counterGuide.title: 1...e5 & ...d5 (Active Center Strike)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Claim central space immediately with 1...e5 and 3...d5, then tuck the knight to b6 and build a solid ...Be7/...Be6 setup.

counterGuide.title: 1...c5 & ...g6 (Symmetrical Fianchetto)
counterGuide.keyIdea: Mirror White's light-square grip with 1...c5 and ...Bg7 so White never gets a free d5 outpost.
